findings.title: updateEvent fallback to destinationCalendar never matches
findings.body:
In `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is computed as:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (undefined/null/empty), the `find` predicate compares each calendar's `externalId` against the same falsy value, which can never be true. The function then resolves to `undefined`, and `calendarId: undefined` is sent to the Google API (the prior behavior of `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` is gone and not replaced by something that actually works). The same defect is duplicated in `deleteEvent` at line 317. Either look up the entry by the current credential id (`cal.credentialId === credentialId`) or use the first array entry when `externalCalendarId` is absent.

findings.title: Team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has no destinationCalendar
createEvent ignores the new credentialId parameter required by the Calendar interface
findings.body: `packages/types/Calendar.d.ts` now declares `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)`. The Lark implementation still has `async createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` and uses only `event.destinationCalendar[0]` to pick a calendar. The same regression exists in `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` (`createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)`) and in `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (`BaseCalendarService.createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)`), which means for collective events where team members use Lark/Office 365/caldav, no credentialId-based selection is performed - only the first entry of `destinationCalendar` is ever consulted, so additional team calendars are never invited. Either implement the credentialId-aware selection in those services or update the shared `Calendar` interface so the implementers don't silently ignore the parameter.

findings.title: createEvent silently falls back to "primary" when destination has no credentialId
findings.body: In `createEvent` the selected calendar is `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`. The `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` integration-based branch calls `createEvent(credential, event)` without `externalId` when a destination entry has no `credentialId`, then `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` is invoked with only the credential id. If that credential isn't represented in `destinationCalendar` (a common case for team-added destinations), `selectedCalendar` is `undefined` and the event is created in the user's "primary" calendar instead of the team host's chosen calendar. This silently creates duplicate/wrong calendar entries for collective Google Calendar bookings.

findings.title: Legacy reference cancel iterates every user calendar credential with the wrong uid/calendar
findings.body: For bookings made before the references refactor, the `else` branch iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter((c) => c.type.endsWith("_calendar"))` and calls `calendar.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)` for *every* calendar credential the user owns, using `uid` and `externalCalendarId` taken from a single reference. With multiple Google/Lark/etc. accounts on the same user, this attempts to delete `uid` from every calendar that never had the event, producing spurious 404s (treated as success) and masking real errors. The inner `for (const credential of calendarCredentials)` should at minimum restrict to the integration type matching `reference.type` (or look up the right calendar in the user's `destinationCalendar`). The PR preserves but doesn't fix this.

findings.title: destinationCalendar fallback to user's destinationCalendar missing
findings.body:
Other handlers in this PR (handleNewBooking, handleCancelBooking, confirm, editLocation, deleteCredential) build `destinationCalendar` as `booking.destinationCalendar ? [booking.destinationCalendar] : user.destinationCalendar ? [user.destinationCalendar] : []`. Here it is just:

```ts
destinationCalendar: bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar
  ? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar]
  : [],
```

A reschedule email for a booking without a per-booking destination calendar (e.g. legacy bookings relying on the user's default) will now deliver `[]` to webhook consumers and the broken-integration email flow, instead of the user's calendar. The fallback to `bookingToReschedule.user?.destinationCalendar` is missing.
